stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking activity around a significant LLM model.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: What’s behind the Google AI shake-up
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: Key personnel departures from Google's AI team, including high-profile figures like Jeff Dean, are reported.
The news raises questions about Google's competitive standing against rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic in AI development.
The shake-up suggests potential internal strategic shifts or challenges within Google's AI research division.

stories.title: ByteDance trains massive AI model in bid to rival Anthropic
stories.author: Zijing Wu, Financial Times
bullet_points: ByteDance (TikTok's parent company) is developing a massive AI model.
The model is reportedly being trained with an enormous scale of 10 trillion parameters.
This effort signals a direct competitive challenge to leading AI labs like Anthropic.

stories.title: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567m over harms to children’s mental health
stories.author: boplicity
bullet_points: A New Mexico court has ordered Meta to pay a substantial sum of $567 million.
The lawsuit centers on alleged harms caused by Meta's platforms to the mental health of children.
This ruling represents a significant legal and regulatory action targeting major social media companies regarding youth safety.

stories.title: AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon
stories.author: itvision
bullet_points: AMD acquired Taalas to enhance AI inference performance.
The core technology involves etching AI models directly into silicon.
This move targets the rapidly expanding market for AI inference solutions.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speedup reaches up to 90% when running with coding agents, based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It integrates native support with Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration leverages MLX, Apple's native machine learning framework, specifically for Apple Silicon.
This represents a significant step toward faster, optimized local AI inference on Apple hardware.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring data processing occurs entirely on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing AI assistance while maintaining user privacy and local control.

stories.title: Microsoft Edge is about to lock out older ad blockers, just like Chrome did
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Microsoft Edge is deprecating support for the Manifest V2 (MV2) extension platform.
This change will effectively block popular ad blockers, such as uBlock Origin, from functioning.
The move mirrors Google Chrome's recent transition away from MV2 extensions.

stories.title: AI chatbots have failed people in crisis. Can that be fixed?
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: AI chatbots have demonstrated failures when interacting with individuals in crisis situations.
Clinicians and researchers are calling for increased transparency regarding AI safety data from tech companies.
The article raises a critical question about the feasibility of fixing these safety failures in AI applications.

stories.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
stories.author: Nuno Vasconcelos
bullet_points: Introduces a novel method for On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPD/OPSD) in LLMs.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods that rely heavily on external supervision (ground truth, feedback).
Achieves genuine 'self'-distillation using only the model's own generations via internal consistency.

stories.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
stories.author: Tabarakul Hazarika
bullet_points: Challenges the standard 'chunk-embed-top-k' paradigm in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for long documents.
Argues the standard approach is structurally unsound for complex, structured documents like financial reports.
Proposes replacing black-box retrieval with more interpretable, agentic operations for better accuracy.

stories.title: Oracle bans AI-generated code from OpenJDK
stories.author: delduca
bullet_points: Oracle is implementing a policy to prohibit the use of AI-generated code within OpenJDK.
This signals a growing concern or stance within the Java ecosystem regarding the quality and provenance of AI-assisted code.
The move represents a potential governance shift in how foundational open-source projects manage AI integration.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to enhance the contextual knowledge of Claude Code.

stories.title: Disney Plus tries a new AI-powered search
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Disney Plus is piloting a new AI-powered search feature.
The new tool supports natural language queries and voice commands for recommendations.
It aims to create customized rows of content based on user input and viewing history.

stories.title: Suno hopes to go legit with watermarks for AI-generated music
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Suno, an AI music generator, is implementing watermarking technology.
The move is intended to combat 'large-scale abuse' of the AI tool.
Download limits are also part of Suno's strategy to control misuse.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark to evaluate context-dependent reasoning.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering better automation and evidence traceability.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of current evaluation methods, which either overspend resources or fail to reach a conclusive result.
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping mechanism, allowing evaluations to stop as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Video Language Models (VLMs) struggle with granular event bookkeeping in real-world video data.
Current benchmarks are criticized for conflating event count, rate, duration, and visual complexity.
The research introduces 'trace-grounded parametric profiling' to accurately audit events against ground truth in controlled tasks.

stories.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
stories.author: Jerzy Stefanowski
bullet_points: The paper addresses critical limitations in the evaluation of Explainable AI (XAI) methods.
It demonstrates challenges using the DetoxAI system for bias detection and concept unlearning in image recognition.
The research explores adapting explanations, such as counterfactuals, to handle concept drift in evolving data streams.

stories.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
stories.author: Juanzi Li
bullet_points: Introduces TRAJDEBUG, a method designed to trace the error lifecycle in complex, long-horizon agent trajectories.
Addresses a critical challenge in LLM-based agentic systems: identifying the earliest root cause of cascading failures.
Highlights the difficulty in debugging long trajectories where evidence for an error can be scattered across distant steps.

stories.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
stories.author: Kristian J. Hammond
bullet_points: Introduces TYTAN, a system designed to automatically construct analytic semantic schemas from relational data.
Addresses the 'knowledge-acquisition bottleneck' where semantic layers are currently manually written, limiting scalability and user accessibility.
Aims to enable natural-language querying and automated report generation by providing data context (entities, measures, relationships).

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to misleading external context signals.
Introduces 'selective trust' as a new paradigm, moving beyond simply training models to ignore all context.
Presents MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test a model's ability to selectively trust context under various conditions.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes a large portion of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with guideline-based clinical reasoning.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering better automation and evidence traceability.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional agent evaluation, which requires an unknown number of games.
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping criterion, allowing evaluation to stop as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered without invalidating confidence levels.

stories.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
stories.author: Kai Jia
bullet_points: Introduces CalibForge, an autonomous system designed for synthesizing terminal tasks in AI.
The system uses adversarial solver calibration to ensure tasks are appropriately challenging for learning agents.
Addresses the gap between task feasibility (solvability) and task relevance (behavior relative to a solver).

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in applying generative reward models (GRMs) to Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core issue identified is the mismatch between GRMs' comparative nature and RL algorithms' scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling the use of GRMs in RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.), not just the model weights.
Automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system—is identified as a crucial, yet challenging, area for AI advancement.
The research highlights a current lack of a standardized protocol within the community for measuring and evaluating these harness optimizations.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark to evaluate context-dependent reasoning.

stories.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
stories.author: Vamse Kumar Subbiah
bullet_points: The paper investigates the shift from LLMs to agents via tool use, specifically focusing on programmatic tool calling (PTC).
PTC is presented as an advancement over rigid JSON tool calls, allowing for natural scripting, chaining, and parallelization in code-capable models.
The research addresses a gap by empirically comparing PTC against native JSON tool calling on established benchmarks under real-world conditions.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluation methods by allowing for certified anytime-valid stopping.
Claims to reduce evaluation costs by a factor of 74 compared to existing methods while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
stories.author: Shujian Huang
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of multilingual reasoning transfer in Large Language Models (LLMs) beyond high-resource languages.
It proposes RP-OPSD, a new method that enhances On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) by explicitly guiding the distillation process with reasoning signals.
The core contribution is characterizing that target-language reasoning involves generating both surface-level and deeper reasoning structures.

stories.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
stories.author: Abigail Goldsteen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of poor quality in existing benchmarks used to evaluate conversational agents.
It introduces a novel, reference-free framework utilizing LLM judges to assess benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.
The framework provides actionable diagnostics to pinpoint weaknesses in current evaluation datasets.

stories.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
stories.author: Tianyong Hao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM evaluation: their performance on rule-intensive document review.
National standard documents (e.g., China GB/T) are used as a complex testbed due to their length, structure, and explicit rules.
Current LLM benchmarks are criticized for focusing too much on domain knowledge and QA, neglecting intrinsic rule adherence.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in applying generative reward models (GRMs) to Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core issue identified is the mismatch between GRM's comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap and unlock GRMs' potential in LLM RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, orchestration, etc.), not just the model weights.
Automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system—is identified as a crucial, yet challenging, area for AI advancement.
The current lack of a common protocol for measuring and benchmarking these harness optimizations is a significant gap in the research community.

stories.title: Making Postgres 300x faster for analytics: batching, operator fusion, and SIMD
stories.author: poly2it
bullet_points: Focuses on significant performance optimization for PostgreSQL, specifically for analytical workloads.
Key techniques mentioned include batching, operator fusion, and the use of SIMD instructions.
Represents an important engineering advancement in database technology, relevant to data infrastructure.

stories.title: How Kiro Crew's Cron Jobs Replaced 4 Hours of Weekly Toil
stories.author: sarvar_04
bullet_points: An AI agent automates several routine developer tasks, including dependency scans and git hygiene checks.
The solution provides automated health reports and end-of-week summaries, significantly reducing manual toil.
The service is presented as a low-cost solution, demonstrated in a short 6-minute video.
